title: The Drowning Glowgarden
story: Deep under the hill lies the Glowgarden, where blind dormice sleep on a mushroom shelf. Pluvigor the Downpipe Drake has curled his wet body into the drain pipe, and storm water is pouring in with nowhere to go. Mr 6 unrolls his siphon-snail hose and starts pumping, cape already soaked.
question: Water is rising in the Glowgarden at 8 inches per minute, while Mr 6's siphon-snail pumps out 5.6 inches per minute. The dormice's shelf sits 18 inches above the water right now. How many minutes until the water reaches the shelf?
solution: The water really gains only 8 - 5.6 = 2.4 inches each minute.
Mr 6 has 7.5 minutes to wake the dormice.
praise: Finding a rate was exactly right — the missing step was subtracting the pumping from the rising before dividing.
hint: Two things happen every minute at once: water pours in and the snail pumps out. What is the water's NET gain in one minute?
victory: Mr 6 carried the sleepy dormice up the ladder with 7.5 minutes to spare, then tickled Pluvigor's tail until the drake popped out of the pipe with a soggy, embarrassed sneeze.
imagePrompt: A brave knightly numeral 6 in a blue cape hauling a coiled siphon hose in a glowing underground mushroom garden as dark water climbs the terraces and a fat drake's tail plugs the drain pipe overhead.
